ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Pablo Neruda

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for an itchy rash on apalutamide

text.paragraph: Mr. Neruda, a 67-year-old man with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer on leuprolide and apalutamide, now in the third week of radiotherapy to the prostate, called the clinic and was seen the same day, with a professional Spanish interpreter. Four days ago an itchy red rash appeared on his chest and spread to his back and upper arms. He has taken apalutamide for eight weeks. He started no other new medicine, soap or detergent. He has no fever, sore mouth, sore or red eyes, blisters, peeling, swelling of the face, or joint pain. The skin over the radiotherapy field on his lower abdomen is not affected. The itch keeps him awake for part of the night, but he is still writing every morning. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-08-10; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well, comfortable; temperature 36.8, blood pressure 136/82, pulse 80

Blanching erythematous macules and papules, merging into patches, over the chest, abdomen above the radiotherapy field, back and upper arms, about 20 percent of body surface; no vesicles, bullae, target lesions, skin pain or Nikolsky sign; face, palms, soles and genitals clear
Mucosa moist and intact; no ulcers
No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Soft and non-tender; no liver enlargement
Urinary frequency, weak stream and nocturia for four months, with right hip and low back pain for six weeks, a hard nodular prostate and a raised PSA; suspected prostate cancer, to be confirmed
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when biopsy and staging established metastatic prostate cancer.

Adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Grade Group 4 (Gleason 4+4), cT3a N1 M1b, de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive disease, low volume by conventional imaging (two bone metastases, in the right ilium and L5, and two pelvic lymph nodes; no visceral disease); synthetic modern detail linked to his documented prostate cancer of 1971
S — Synthetic grade, stage, extent and PSA; the prostate cancer and the operation in France in 1971 are documented (D), and no stage, grade or treatment detail was found in the sources read.
Bone metastases from prostate cancer: right iliac wing (painful) and L5 vertebral body; no cord compression
Pelvic lymph node metastases: right external iliac and right obturator nodes
S — Synthetic status in the modern episode.

Continuous androgen deprivation (leuprolide) with apalutamide, with monitoring of testosterone, PSA, thyroid function, blood pressure, glucose and lipids, bone health, rash, falls, hot flashes, sexual health, mood and cognition
S — Synthetic treatment plan; Z79.899 is used because ICD-10-CM has no specific code for GnRH agonist therapy.
Essential hypertension for five years, on amlodipine
S — Synthetic comorbidity, relevant to cardiovascular risk on androgen deprivation; not a claim about his real blood pressure.
S — Synthetic finding at intake, addressed at the second visit.
Low bone mass (femoral neck T-score -2.1, L1 to L4 -1.4) with a ten-year hip fracture risk above 3% (FRAX, with androgen deprivation counted as a cause of secondary osteoporosis)
S — Synthetic bone-health finding on the DXA before androgen deprivation.
S — Synthetic metabolic finding at intake, relevant to androgen deprivation.

Maculopapular drug rash from apalutamide, grade 2 (about 20 percent of body surface, trunk and upper arms), eight weeks into treatment; no mucosal involvement, blistering, fever, eosinophilia or liver involvement; settled on topical steroid and an antihistamine without stopping apalutamide
S — Synthetic intercurrent problem at an unscheduled visit; a known effect of apalutamide, not a historical claim.

list.item:
Apalutamide rash, grade 2 (L27.0). A maculopapular drug rash, a common effect of apalutamide, covering about 20 percent of the skin: grade 2 (10 to 30 percent). No features of a severe reaction: no mucosal sores, blisters or skin pain, no fever, no lymph nodes, eosinophils 0.3, and normal liver and kidney tests (ALT 27, AST 26, creatinine 0.97). Grade 2 rash does not require stopping apalutamide, and most such rashes settle on topical treatment. [S]
Continue apalutamide 240 mg daily.
Triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily for two weeks to the rash, not the face or groin, and a fragrance-free emollient.
Cetirizine 10 mg daily for itch.
Stop apalutamide and call the same day for blisters, peeling, mouth or eye sores, fever, or spread beyond a third of the skin.
Medical oncology informed today; radiotherapy continues.

Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (C61). Third week of radiotherapy to the prostate; urinary frequency as expected; no bone pain. [S]
Three-month review as planned in five weeks.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Prostate Cancer (2026); ERLEADA (apalutamide) tablets: prescribing information (2026)

Follow-up: Nurse telephone call in three days, with a photograph of the rash through the patient portal if he wishes. Three-month review in five weeks. Same-day review for any of the warning signs. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-14: three-month review: PSA and testosterone, thyroid function, blood count and chemistry, glucose, radiotherapy effects, the rash, the second leuprolide injection, and plans for the year. [S]
